identity.name: Commonwealth of England
alt_names: Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland

land.text: England, which 'An Act declaring England to be a Commonwealth' (19 May 1649) turned into a republic; Cliopatria's Commonwealth shape of 1645-1648 is Parliament's England and Wales

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws the Parliamentarian side of the civil wars under this row from 1645, four years before the Commonwealth was declared; the researcher dates the state from 19 May 1649 (see notes).

minus.text: England and Wales under the restored monarchy

land.text: England and Wales: the restored monarchy of Charles II ('On 8 May 1660, the Convention Parliament declared Charles II the lawful successor of Charles I and king'; Charles II returned on 23 May 1660 and entered London on 29 May), without Scotland and without Ireland

successors.note: Scotland passes back to the Kingdom of Scotland (kingdom-of-scotland) in 1660; Cliopatria has no Kingdom of England shape for 1661 and draws this row to 1661. [fx-42: without Ireland, which kingdom-of-england does not draw (its 1660-1707 corrections subtract the island) and which goes to kingdom-of-ireland.]

land.text: the whole island of Ireland, with the Galway, Dundalk and Clew Bay cells that kingdom-of-england's corrections cut out: the Crown's Kingdom of Ireland restored in 1660

successors.note: Ireland was held by the Commonwealth from 1652-1653 ('England, Scotland and Ireland were ruled as a republic until 1660', Kingdom of Ireland page, infobox 'Commonwealth: 1652-1660') and returns to its own kingdom at the Restoration ('The kingdom's order was restored 1660 with the restoration of Charles II'; infobox 'Dependency of England (1542-1707)'). Added fx-42, 2 Nov 2026, for R074; kingdom-of-ireland ledger/14 (1660, 'split' from the Commonwealth) moves no land to Ireland, because a split gives the splitting state's own cells away.

capitals.name: London (Westminster)
capitals.note: The Commonwealth page's infobox gives no capital; London is the researcher's reading (the same page has Charles II enter London on 29 May 1660 and the Rump Parliament, Council of State and Protectors govern from there).

rulers.name: Oliver Cromwell
rulers.title: Lord Protector
rulers.note: Sworn in as Lord Protector on 16 December 1653; died in September 1658. The Commonwealth of 1649-1653 had no single ruler (Rump Parliament and Council of State).

correction.text: unchanged shape (England and Wales); years change: this shape is Parliament's England and Wales from the end of the First Civil War (Oxford, 24 June 1646; Harlech, 13 March 1647) and belongs to the Commonwealth only from 19 May 1649; in 1645 the page has the Royalists holding 'most of the West Country, Wales, and counties along the English border'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 138,621 km2 England-and-Wales shape (1645-1647) is Parliament's side of the First Civil War, not the Commonwealth: the page has the New Model Army created in February 1645, Naseby on 14 June 1645, and 'the Royalists still controlled most of the West Country, Wales, and counties along the English border' in early 1645; Oxford capitulated on 24 June 1646 and Harlech held out until 13 March 1647. The shape is therefore Parliament's only from mid-1646/1647 and the Commonwealth is not proclaimed until 19 May 1649 (Commonwealth of England page): the researcher keeps the shape but moves its owner and years (see notes). Infobox area: none on the page; the shape (England 142,636 km2 on the gazetteer grid, Wales about 13,600 km2 inside it) is consistent with England and Wales.

Baseline for 1648-1652: England and Wales plus about 14,000 km2 of Ireland (Ulster 30 cells, Leinster 21, Munster 4 on the grid), consistent with the page's 'the only remaining Parliamentarian outpost in Ireland was in Dublin' by 1649 plus Charles Coote's army 'based around Derry'; the Munster cells are not supported by any page opened. The Irish conquest of 1649-1653 and the Scottish conquest of 1650-1652 are carried by the ledger gains (Kilkenny and Waterford 1650, Limerick 1651, the Lowlands 1651, Galway 1652, Scotland 1652), not by this shape. Infobox area: none on the Commonwealth page.

341,676 km2: all of England, Wales, Scotland (324 of 330 grid cells) and Ireland (341 of 344), i.e. the 'Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland' of 1653; the Protectorate page says 'By the end of 1653, the Protectorate was in the unique position of being the first government in history to be in control of the entirety of the British Isles'. No infobox area on the page; the modern British Isles (United Kingdom 243,600 km2 plus Ireland 70,300 km2) is 314,000 km2, ratio 1.09. The shape holds for 1653-1658 although the Tender of Union is dated 12 April 1654.

correction.text: unchanged shape; the years end in 1660 (the Stuart Restoration of May 1660), not 1661

keyframe_review.note: Same 341,494 km2 shape; the years end in 1660, not 1661: the Convention Parliament proclaimed Charles II on 8 May 1660 and he returned on 23 May 1660 (page), and Cliopatria's Kingdom of England shape begins in 1662. The Rump was recalled in May 1659 after Richard Cromwell's resignation on 25 May 1659 (Protectorate page), so 1659-1660 is the restored Commonwealth with the same territory.

region.text: England, declared a Commonwealth by the Rump Parliament

ledger.note: 1649: the Rump Parliament declares England a Commonwealth (19 May). Infobox 'Established: 19 May 1649, when the Rump Parliament adopted An Act declaring England to be a Commonwealth.' The page names England; Wales is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Ireland, which the Commonwealth moved 'to retake' after the execution of Charles I in January 1649

ledger.note: 1649: Cromwell lands at Dublin to reconquer Ireland (15 August). 'Cromwell landed near Dublin in August 1649 with an expeditionary force'; the infobox dates the campaign 15 August 1649 to 27 September 1653. The Confederates were allied with the Royalists under Ormonde (a combined force was beaten at Rathmines on 2 August); Parliament held only Dublin and, under Coote, the Derry area.

region.text: Waterford, which surrendered after a prolonged siege in 1650

ledger.note: 1650: Waterford and Duncannon fall. 'Waterford and Duncannon eventually surrendered after prolonged sieges in 1650.' Duncannon fort stands in Wexford, outside the region named.

1650: Kilkenny, the Confederate capital, is captured in March. 'Kilkenny was captured in March 1650'; the Cromwellian conquest page puts Kilkenny and Clonmel in Cromwell's 'following spring' mopping-up of 'the remaining walled towns in Ireland's southeast'.

1650: Cromwell invades Scotland (22 July). 'On 22 July the New Model Army under Oliver Cromwell invaded Scotland'; he beat the Scots at Dunbar on 3 September 1650. Scotland had proclaimed Charles II, which is why the Commonwealth moved against it.
1651: Limerick falls. 'Limerick fell in 1651' (Ireton died of plague outside it); the page puts the Shannon crossing into Connacht in October 1650.

region.text: Perth, Stirling, Alyth, St Andrews and Dundee, taken between July and 1 September 1651

ledger.note: 1651: the central Lowlands fall. Perth, the seat of the Scottish government, was marched on on 31 July 1651; 'By the end of August, Monck had captured Stirling, Alyth, and St Andrews'; 'the English stormed the west and east ports' of Dundee on 1 September 1651; Charles II's army was destroyed at Worcester on 3 September 1651. The page names towns, not provinces: the region is the researcher's reading.

1652: Galway falls in May and organised Confederate resistance ends. 'Galway was captured in May 1652'; the Cromwellian page has 'Galway the following year' (1652) and Irish guerrilla leaders surrendering 'under terms signed at Kilkenny that May'.

1652: the last Scottish strongholds surrender. Dunnottar Castle 'was the last major Scottish stronghold to surrender, on 24 May 1652'; Brodick Castle had surrendered on 6 April and the Bass Rock a few days later. The page's conflict span is 1650-1652.

region.text: Scotland, conquered by 1652 and incorporated in the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland

ledger.note: 1652: Scotland is conquered. Dunnottar (24 May 1652) is the last major stronghold; the Kingdom of Scotland page calls 1653-1660 the 'short-lived incorporation of Scotland into the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland', and the Protectorate page has the Scottish Parliament 'permanently dissolved' with 30 seats at Westminster. Cliopatria draws Scotland in the Commonwealth from 1653. Union followed in law: 'On 12 April 1654, under the terms of the Tender of Union, the Ordinance for uniting Scotland into one Commonwealth with England was issued' and it became an Act on 26 June 1657 (Protectorate page).

region.text: the rest of Ireland: the Confederate-Royalist lands of Connacht and the west, whose forces 'surrendered in 1652, under terms signed at Kilkenny that May'

ledger.note: May 1652: the last Confederate land passes to the Commonwealth. Irish guerrilla forces 'surrendered in 1652, under terms signed at Kilkenny that May' (Cromwellian conquest page) and Galway was captured in May 1652 (Irish Confederate Wars page); sporadic guerrilla warfare went on until 1653 (contest to 27 September 1653) and Ireland was formally merged into the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland in 1653. Reviewer eu-11-j moved this gain from September 1653 to May 1652 (confidence 3 to 2) to match the irish-catholic-confederation dissolve of May 1652, whose land would otherwise have no owner for sixteen months.

1653: the Irish war ends (27 September). Parliament declared the rebellion subdued on 27 September 1653 (infobox: campaign 15 August 1649 - 27 September 1653); 'The last organised Irish force surrendered in Cavan in April 1653' and Cloughoughter surrendered on 27 April 1653.
1653: Cromwell becomes Lord Protector (16 December): the Protectorate, officially the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland, lasts until 25 May 1659. Same state and colour (rule 2).

June 1658: Dunkirk is handed to the Protectorate. 'After the Battle of the Dunes (1658), the town of Dunkirk was awarded by France to the Protectorate' (The Protectorate page); the battle was fought on 14 June 1658 near Dunkirk 'in what was then the Spanish Netherlands', the port surrendered to the French on 24 June and 'Cardinal Mazarin honoured the terms of the treaty with Oliver Cromwell and handed the port over to the Commonwealth' (Battle of the Dunes page). Charles II sold it back to France in 1662. A continental enclave outside every Cliopatria shape. Month and source added by reviewer eu-11-j.

1659: Richard Cromwell resigns (25 May) and the Rump Parliament is recalled: the Commonwealth is restored until 1660. The Protectorate lasted 'from 16 December 1653 to 25 May 1659'; a new Council of State was named on 19 May 1659.

1660: Scotland leaves the Commonwealth with the Restoration; the Kingdom of Scotland page ends the 'incorporation of Scotland into the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland (1653-1660)'. The page gives the period, not the month.

minus.text: England and Wales under the restored monarchy

region.text: England and Wales pass to Charles II's restored monarchy; Scotland goes back to its own kingdom and Ireland to the kingdom of Ireland (the island with the Galway, Dundalk and Clew Bay cells that kingdom-of-england's own corrections cut out)

ledger.note: 1660: the Stuart Restoration ends the Commonwealth. 'On 8 May 1660, the Convention Parliament declared Charles II the lawful successor of Charles I and king'; he returned from exile on 23 May and entered London on 29 May (the infobox gives only 1660 for the end). [Repair fx-42, 2 Nov 2026 (dossier request R074): Ireland no longer goes to kingdom-of-england. The compiler hands a dying state's cells to its successors by identity.successors land, so the island went to kingdom-of-england in 1660, kingdom-of-england's 1662 keyframe (minus Ireland) released it to nobody and Ireland stayed empty to 1691. Kingdom of Ireland page: 'England, Scotland and Ireland were ruled as a republic until 1660', 'The kingdom's order was restored 1660 with the restoration of Charles II', infobox 'Dependency of England (1542-1707)'. The loss event of May 1660 is not repeated here: p1660-p1669 events/3 already carries it.]

wars.name: Cromwellian conquest of Ireland
belligerents: Royalists under the Marquess of Ormonde

zones.text: all of Ireland; Dublin and the Derry area held by Parliament at the start

wars.outcome: Commonwealth victory: Kilkenny (March 1650), Waterford (1650), Limerick (1651) and Galway (May 1652) fall; the last organised force surrenders at Cloughoughter on 27 April 1653 and Parliament declares the rebellion subdued on 27 September 1653; Ireland is merged into the Commonwealth.
wars.note: Infobox 15 August 1649 - 27 September 1653. The page gives no date for Drogheda or Wexford or for Cromwell's departure (the outbreak of the Anglo-Scottish war forced him to leave).

wars.name: Anglo-Scottish War (Third English Civil War)

zones.text: Scotland: Dunbar 3 September 1650, Perth 1651, Dundee 1 September 1651, Dunnottar 24 May 1652

wars.outcome: Commonwealth victory: Dunbar (3 September 1650), Inverkeithing (20 July 1651), Worcester (3 September 1651) and the fall of Dunnottar (24 May 1652) end Scottish independence; Scotland is incorporated in the Commonwealth.
wars.note: The page's war article is titled Third English Civil War (the Anglo-Scottish War (1650-1652) URL does not exist).

wars.name: Battle of the Dunes and the Dunkirk award
wars.outcome: Franco-English victory: 'the town of Dunkirk was awarded by France to the Protectorate'; sold back to France by Charles II in 1662.
wars.note: The Protectorate page gives no dates for the Anglo-Spanish War or the Jamaica expedition (Western Design); only the Battle of the Dunes (1658).

certainty.note: The Irish and Scottish fronts move year by year (Kilkenny 1650, Limerick 1651, Dunnottar and Galway 1652); only the English coast and the border of 1237 (Treaty of York, Kingdom of Scotland page) are fixed.
One state over the whole of the British Isles, with island coasts as its borders; Dunkirk (1658) is an enclave of uncertain extent.

notes:
Written by eu-11-j on 2026-10-25 from the pages listed (5 core pages plus the Irish Confederate Wars and Kingdom of Scotland pages opened for neighbouring dossiers).

BIGGEST DECISION FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: Cliopatria runs this row 1645-1661, but the Commonwealth was proclaimed on 19 May 1649 and ended in May 1660. The dossier dates the state 1649-1660 (found/dissolve events agree). The 1645-1648 shape (Parliament's England and Wales, 138,621 km2) is kept and reviewed as 'adjust' (years/owner change). If the renderers clamp shapes to the state's life, England and Wales are blank in 1645-1648 unless the kingdom-of-england dossier (group eu-11, not mine) carries Parliament's England for those years; its Cliopatria shapes for 1645-1652 are only the royalist remnant (70,537 km2 in 1645-47, 20,067 km2 of Ireland in 1648-52). Either start this dossier in 1645 or have the England dossier cover 1642-1649.

Scotland and Ireland in the shape: the 1653 shape contains all of Scotland and Ireland, but the pages date the conquest in steps (Ireland 1649-1653, Scotland 1650-1652). Those steps are in the ledger as gains/contests; the 1648 baseline does not include them.

Not settled (pages silent): Drogheda and Wexford (dated by memory only, not recorded); Jamaica (Western Design) and the Anglo-Spanish War (the Protectorate page gives no dates); the Channel Islands, Isle of Man and Scilly under the Commonwealth (no page opened mentions them); the 1648 baseline's Munster cells; the date of the Irish union (page says 1653-59). The Ordinance of Union (12 April 1654) and the Act of 26 June 1657 are in the note of the 1652 Scotland gain, not a `merge` event, because Scotland returns to its own kingdom in 1660.

Counterparts needing dossiers from others: kingdom-of-england (the Parliamentarian state of 1642-1649 and the Restoration), kingdom-of-scotland (mine), irish-catholic-confederation (mine), kingdom-of-france (eu-10, Dunkirk 1658), Spain (Dunkirk, Anglo-Spanish War), a Kingdom of Ireland (Ormonde's royalist Ireland 1649; eu-11-x).
Region names the gazetteer lacks: none besides the lon/lat radius used for Dunkirk (no 'Dunkirk' place).
Fix pass fx-42 (2 Nov 2026), dossier request R074: ledger/16 (dissolve) and the kingdom-of-england successor now exclude Ireland, and kingdom-of-ireland is a second successor with the island, so the Irish land no longer passes to kingdom-of-england at the end of 1660 and is no longer released to nobody by that state's 1662 keyframe. The May 1660 loss event itself is carried by data/patches/p1660-p1669.json events/3 and is not repeated. Handoff for kingdom-of-ireland: ledger/14 (1660 split, counterpart commonwealth-of-england) gives the island's cells to the Commonwealth instead of taking them; a gain would be the right type.
